title: Rebuild CultureMech memberships for split trace-solution identities
body:
## Problem

Trace-element stock solutions have been split off the generic `NCIT:C896` identifier:

- `MIM:Trace_Element_Solution_SL-10` -> `kgmicrobe.ingredient:trace_element_solution_sl-10`
- `MIM:Trace_Element_Solution` -> `kgmicrobe.ingredient:trace_element_solution`
- `MIM:Zeikus_Trace_Element_Solution` -> `kgmicrobe.ingredient:zeikus_trace_element_solution`

The tracked CultureMech recipe-membership artifact still publishes eight edges under the old shared identifier:

```text
mappings/culturemech_recipe_membership.tsv:190421-190428
NCIT:C896    CultureMech:013208    1
...
NCIT:C896    CultureMech:014194    1
```

After the split, no live MIM record owns `NCIT:C896`, and future runs of `scripts/build_culturemech_membership.py` will classify matching occurrence rows as unknown until `src/mediaingredientmech/utils/culturemech_occurrences.py` has exact source-label overrides for the split trace-solution labels.

## Follow-up

- Add exact `SOURCE_LABEL_IDENTIFIER_OVERRIDES` for the trace-solution source labels that CultureMech still resolves to `NCIT:C896`.
- Rebuild `mappings/culturemech_recipe_membership.tsv` from the CultureMech `ingredient_occurrences.tsv` snapshot used for the membership artifact.
- Add or extend a guard so every published `mim_identifier` in `mappings/culturemech_recipe_membership.tsv` is held by at least one active MIM record.
- Reconcile the three trace-solution records' `occurrence_statistics` with the source-label-specific membership edges so these local stock-solution identities do not inherit one shared parent count.

Found during adversarial review of #559.
